title: Rajasthan Counted Voters Thrice In Under a Year. The Numbers Changed Every Time.
shows: The Wire sets side by side the three counts of Rajasthan's electors made in 2026. The final roll of the Special Intensive Revision held 5.15 crore electors, the draft roll of the special summary revision now under way holds 5.26 crore, and the State Election Commission's final roll for the panchayat and municipal elections holds 5.45 crore. It explains that the Election Commission prepares the rolls for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections under Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950, while State Election Commissions prepare the rolls for panchayat and municipal elections under Articles 243K and 243ZA. It reports, from the Times of India, that the State Election Commission's secretary Rajesh Verma said his office built its rolls from the Commission's roll of 1 January 2025, from before the revision, because preparations for the local elections began before the revision was over. It cites a comparison by Nikhil Dey, a founder of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, which found 26.63 lakh electors deleted in the revision still on the State Election Commission's local body rolls, and his question how people the revision found dead could be on the state's roll. It notes that the claims and objections of the summary revision may change the count again by January 2027.
quote: The Rajasthan SEC secretary, Rajesh Verma, confirmed separately to the Times of India that the SEC used the pre-SIR ECI electoral roll, last updated on January 1, 2025, to prepare its voter lists.
note: First reading, 14 November 2026. Read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) with curl on 14 November 2026. Published 13 November 2026 at 8:02 pm IST (post_date_gmt 14:32:47), byline The Wire Staff, New Delhi. The three counts check against the site. The final roll of 21 February 2026 is 5,15,19,929 for 199 seats and the summary revision's draft of 12 November is 5,26,67,416 (data/india/raw/final.csv and ssr_draft.csv). The draft is about 11 lakh above the final roll, as the Times of India report The Wire quotes says. The Wire then writes that the gap is closer to 19 lakh, and later that the State Election Commission's count differs by 19 lakh from the revision's. Both should read the summary revision's draft, since 5.45 crore less 5.26 crore is 19 lakh and the State Election Commission's count is 30 lakh above the revision's final roll, which The Wire also states. The summary is written from the figures and does not repeat the slip. The Wire also calls all 26.63 lakh 'deceased' voters in one sentence. Dey's figure is of electors deleted for any reason, and PUCL's analysis reported by the Times of India on 14 November (on this list) puts those marked dead at about 3.2 lakh, so the summary says deleted. The 26.63 lakh is close to PUCL's earlier figure of nearly 26.7 lakh from the panchayat rolls of 25 February as the Times of India gives it, and The Wire does not say which rolls Dey compared. Amar Ujala's report of Dey's account is soft-57 and The Reporters' Collective's count of 1,82,440 electors marked dead who are on the panchayat roll is soft-59.

title: 26L deleted in Rajasthan post-SIR still on panchayat poll rolls: PUCL
shows: The Times of India reports an analysis by the People's Union for Civil Liberties, dated 11 November, which found that more than 26 lakh of the 41.65 lakh electors deleted from Rajasthan's draft roll in the Special Intensive Revision are still on the State Election Commission's rolls for the 2026 panchayat and urban local body elections, 13.7 lakh on the panchayat rolls and 12.4 lakh on the municipal rolls. The analysis covers the State Election Commission's second supplement to the panchayat rolls, published up to 12 October. By PUCL's count these include 3,20,395 people the Election Commission marked dead, more than 17.32 lakh it deleted as shifted, 3.67 lakh as untraceable or absent and more than 1.83 lakh as enrolled elsewhere. Baran has the highest share of deleted electors still on the State Election Commission's rolls, 83.1%, followed by Pali, Jalore, Bikaner, Sirohi and Deedwana-Kuchaman, all above 80%. Of those marked dead, 70.7% in Banswara are still on the rolls, and PUCL says at least half are in seven districts. The figure is 69,343 lower than PUCL's earlier count of nearly 26.7 lakh from the panchayat rolls of 25 February, and the number marked dead and still listed fell by 31,987 from 3,52,382. PUCL puts the active names across the State Election Commission's rolls at 5,47,86,896, which is 32,72,934 or 6.4% more than the Election Commission's final roll of 5,15,13,962. The State Election Commission's secretary Rajesh Verma told the paper that the state's roll numbers have increased in recent months and that the update process likely reduced the gap.
quote: The analysis further reported that 3.2 lakh people identified as dead by ECI continued to be on SEC rolls statewide.
"The reduction in the discrepancy between the two lists likely happened in the update process," Verma said.
note: First reading, 14 November 2026. Read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 14 November 2026, which marks the article isAccessibleForFree true. Byline Siddhartha Dutta, Jaipur, datePublished 2026-11-14T00:57:00+05:30. PUCL's analysis itself was not found, and every figure is PUCL's as the paper reports it. The arithmetic holds. 13.7 lakh and 12.4 lakh add to just over 26 lakh, the four reasons (17.32, 3.67, 1.83 and 3.2 lakh) add to about 26.0 lakh, 3,52,382 less 3,20,395 is 31,987, and 5,47,86,896 less 5,15,13,962 is 32,72,934, which is 6.35% of the final roll. The paper gives the October supplement as removing 69,578 deleted names, 32,027 of them marked dead, and the net falls as 69,343 and 31,987, which it does not reconcile. The paper says the analysis also counts 2.3 lakh names the State Election Commission added. PUCL's 41.65 lakh deleted differs from the site's 41,84,891 for 199 seats (data/india/states.json), and its final roll of 5,15,13,962 is 5,967 below the site's 5,15,19,929 from the Chief Electoral Officer's fact sheet of 21 February. The report does not say which base PUCL used. The district figures for those marked dead (Sirohi 67.5%, Baran 61.4%, Churu 55.8%, Jalore 54.4%, Ajmer 51.1%, Bikaner 50.8%) are not all carried. The Reporters' Collective's count of 1,82,440 electors marked dead who are on the panchayat roll is soft-59, and Amar Ujala's report of Nikhil Dey's account is soft-57.
